blogs.title: The Pre-op Trap: Why Early Post-CABG Thrombocytopenia Demands a HIT Workup Before Day 5
blogs.description: This post explores the critical diagnostic pitfall of dismissing thrombocytopenia occurring earlier than the classic POD5-10 window following cardiac surgery. Using the case study, we analyze how preoperative heparin exposure (even a small 'flush' dose during catheterization) can prime the immune system, leading to rapid-onset HIT within 24 hours of re-exposure during surgery. We discuss the '4 Ts' score nuances in the early postoperative setting and why a low threshold for ordering PF4/EIA and SRA is essential to prevent catastrophic stroke.

blogs.title: Decoding the Indeterminate SRA: Recognizing Autoimmune HIT Through Atypical Serology
blogs.description: Moving beyond standard textbook definitions, this article dissects a unique serotonin-release assay (SRA) profile where platelet activation occurred at zero heparin concentration and demonstrated partial resistance to Fc-receptor blockade (monoclonal antibody IV.3). We explain why these 'atypical' results are actually pathognomonic for autoimmune HIT (aHIT), how to interpret them when labs flag them as 'indeterminate,' and why missing this specific serological signature can lead to misdiagnosis or delayed initiation of appropriate therapy.

blogs.title: When Argatroban Fails: Managing Severe Hypercoagulability and Consumptive Coagulopathy in aHIT
blogs.description: While argatroban is a standard first-line agent for HIT, this case illustrates scenarios where it may be insufficient to control the profound hypercoagulable state associated with severe autoimmune HIT. We examine the warning signs of persistent consumption (falling fibrinogen, rising D-dimers, new schistocytes) despite therapeutic INR/PTT targets. The discussion focuses on the strategic switch to fondaparinux, the necessity of checking antithrombin levels before administration, and the role of adjunctive therapies like high-dose IVIG in refractory cases.

blogs.title: From Stroke Recovery to Long-Term Management: Navigating Anticoagulation Transition in Post-HIT Patients
blogs.description: Focusing on the discharge planning and long-term care for a patient surviving severe HIT with thrombotic complications. This post reviews the timeline of platelet recovery in this case (reaching normal counts by POD62) and analyzes the decision-making process for transitioning from parenteral agents back to oral anticoagulation. We address the specific challenge of managing atrial fibrillation in a patient with recent stroke and active HIT antibodies, weighing options between DOACs (apixaban) versus warfarin or continued LMWH/fondaparinux during the convalescent phase.
